turns.content: I'm planning my first trip to Japan. Any advice on where to go?
A classic first-timer route: Tokyo → Kyoto → Osaka. Gives you the urban buzz, the traditional culture, and the food culture all at once.
How long would I need for that?
Ten to fourteen days is comfortable. Tokyo alone could take five days — the neighborhoods are so distinct they almost feel like separate cities.
What time of year is best?
March–April for cherry blossom season, but it's crowded and pricey. October–November has incredible autumn foliage and milder crowds.
Should I get a JR Pass?
Do the math first. The 14-day pass is worth it if you're doing the full Tokyo–Kyoto–Osaka loop plus any Shinkansen side trips. Otherwise single tickets can be cheaper.
What about accommodation — hotels or ryokan?
Mix both. At least one or two nights in a ryokan in Kyoto is non-negotiable — it's a whole ritual with kaiseki dinner and an onsen bath.

Mid-range. Food is surprisingly affordable — some of the best meals I've heard about were convenience store breakfast and a 700-yen ramen bowl. Transport and accommodation add up, but you get extraordinary value for the quality.
Any apps I should download before I go?
Google Translate with Japanese downloaded offline, Google Maps, and Hyperdia for train schedules. IC Card (Suica or Pasmo) on your iPhone or Android if your phone supports it.
This is super helpful. What's the one thing people regret not doing?
Leaving time to wander without a plan. The best experiences in Japan tend to happen when you turn down an unmarked alley.
